message:
added else-block for if-block on line #699

Added missing else-block for the if-block ```if norm != "NONE":``` on line #699. Added else-block sets ```c1Norm``` and ```c2Norm``` to ```None```. 

Calls to ```c1Norm``` and ```c2Norm``` include those in:
- ```normalizematrix.__init__``` (which sets ```c1Norm``` and ```c2Norm``` as instance parameters)
- ```normalizematrix.getDataFromBinRegion``` (which passed ```c1Norm``` and ```c2Norm``` as arguments to multiprocessed calls to ```readBlockWorker```)
- ```readBlockWorker``` (which only uses ```c1Norm``` and ```c2Norm``` in an if-block: ```if norm != "NONE"```)

author: Alexandre Moine <alexandre@moine.me>
message:
Rewrite rules for bind (#157)

This commit defines `fmap` in terms of `bind` and adds a test to make sure that `fmap f . fmap g` is rewritten to `fmap (f.g)` by the rewrite rules.

This change reflects that `fmap` can be expressed with `bind` and `bind` can be fused with `foldg`. Moreover, any function preserving the structure of the graph (like `fmap`) can be expressed with `bind`, so this is an "optimal" change, since we do not have to add any other rule for structure preserving-functions.

author: Jonathan Dowland <jon@dow.land>
message:
Export.Dot: Extend Style to define Quoting styles

GraphViz supports different types of label. The type is determined by
the delimiters used to quote the label's value. Double-quotes denote
a literal string. Pairs of angle brackets ("<>") denote a "HTML-like"
string, which permits the use of (some) HTML mark-up in the graph.

Extend the `Style` record type to include a `quoting` field, to signal
whether or not attribute values should be double-quoted. A user wishing
to use another quote style must define their style's quoting attribute
as `NoQuote` and then ensure their attribute values contain embedded
quote characters of their choice.

Adjust `defaultStyle` and the `attributes` function accordingly and add
a test.

Fixes #272.

Signed-off-by: Jonathan Dowland <jon@dow.land>

author: Jonathan Dowland <jon@dow.land>
message:
escape strings to satisfy Dot syntax rules

GraphViz's "dot" language has several options for encoding IDs, as
described here: https://www.graphviz.org/doc/info/lang.html

Alga makes use of the quoted-string syntax. This permits any character
within double quotes, except the double-quote character itself, which
must be prefixed by a backslash character. (the backslash itself does
not need to be escaped).

Implement the escaping of " for defaultStyleViaShow.

author: Patrick Hilhorst <git@hilhorst.be>
message:
Use faster algorithm for components

Benchmarks
==========

These benchmarks were done with the following program:

```haskell
import           Algebra.Graph                (Graph)
import           Algebra.Graph.NonEmpty       (components, vertexCount)
import           Algebra.Graph.Test.Arbitrary
import           Data.Foldable
import qualified Data.Set                     as S
import           Test.QuickCheck
import           Test.QuickCheck.Gen
import           Test.QuickCheck.Random

genSeed seed (MkGen g) =
  do let r = mkQCGen seed
     return (g r 30)

main :: IO ()
main = do
  let gen = (resize 100 $ arbitrary) :: Gen (Graph Int)
  for_ [1..1000] $ \seed -> do
    g <- genSeed seed gen
    print (vertexCount <$> (S.toList $ components g))
```

Ran on my own laptop. Not very scientific, but better than nothing, and
the improvement is clear.

The improvements mostly seem to be in the worst-case performance. When not
using a fixed seed, times varied drastically.

This does introduce a new dependency, but I think the speed improvement is
worth it.

5 graphs of depth 1000
----------------------

**New**

    14.91user 0.04system 0:14.96elapsed 99%CPU (0avgtext+0avgdata 30688maxresident)k
    0inputs+0outputs (0major+19991minor)pagefaults 0swaps

**Old**

    188.67user 0.44system 3:09.12elapsed 99%CPU (0avgtext+0avgdata 31592maxresident)k
    0inputs+0outputs (0major+18148minor)pagefaults 0swaps

12x improvement

7408maxresident)k 0inputs+0outputs (0major+945minor)pagefaults 0swaps

message:
Implement shrinking for adjancency maps

We implement shrinking for

- AdjacencyMap
- AdjacencyIntMap
- Labelled.AdjacencyMap
- NonEmpty.AdjacencyMap

The shrinking strategy is limited but reasonably effective. Give a graph
g we produce a list of subgraphs of g obtained by removing one vertex
and then one edge at a time.

author: Xavier Bouthillier <xavier.bouthillier@gmail.com>
message:
Add hashing to environment (#94)

Why:

Hashing an environment makes it possible to verify if two initial states
are identical. This is necessary if we want to create groups of initial
states that are mutually exclusive.

How:

Compute the hash of the grid encoding with the initial agent position and
direction.

Note:

I'm not sure if the RNG state may eventually cause divergences in the
episodes and whether that should be accounted for in the hashing. It's
difficult to measure however the divergence without playing, and taking
into account the RNG state will likely give different hashing for
practically identical states. That's why my feeling is the RNG state should not
be part of the hashing.

author: Xavier Bouthillier <xavier.bouthillier@umontreal.ca>
message:
Add hashing to environment

Why:

Hashing an environment makes it possible to verify if two initial states
are identical. This is necessary if we want to create groups of initial
states that are mutually exclusive.

How:

Compute the hash of the grid encoding with the initial agent position and
direction.

Note:

I'm not sure if the RNG state may eventually cause divergences in the
episodes and whether that should be accounted for in the hashing. It's
difficult to measure however the divergence without playing, and taking
into account the RNG state will likely give different hashing for
practically identical states. That's why my feeling is the RNG state should not
be part of the hashing.

 * update `Grid.encode` to take an optional `vis_mask` argument, and
 return an image which now distinguishes between unseen and empty cells
 (values respectively 0 and 1).

 * update `Grid.decode` to handle the above changes;  values 0 and 1 in
 input array are both mapped to None in output grid.

 * make Grid.decode() a static method;  it was already used as a static
 method but was missing the appropriate decorator.

 * update "observation encode/decode roundtrip" test in run_tests.py;
 the visualization mask necessary to perform the test is found by
 manually checking the first channel of the image for value 0.

message:
feat: add use_byte_offsets to cv.mesh.get

    The manifest for sharded is a bit strange in that exists(..., return_byte_offset=True)
    is being called on the server side. To avoid duplicative delay by recomputing the offset
    locations, the manifest breaks encapsulation by returning the shard filename and byte
    offsets. This breaks enapsulation of the shard fetching logic rather severely.

    In order to support fetching meshes in more extraordinary conditions, such as when
    developing a second mesh with different shard parameters while maintaining the older
    mesh for proofreading and visualization while it's generated, we incoroprate a hybrid
    mode that continues to use the manifest, but in order to acquire labels and then fetches
    the labels in bypass mode.

Per personal communication dated Aug. 29, JBMS indicated

of the data segments that it is attempting to point to.

author: William Silversmith <william.silversmith@gmail.com>
message:
perf: 1x memory usage for parallel downloads (#112)

Previously, I was very conservative and wanted to ensure
that the usage of shared memory was completely invisible
to the end user of downloaded numpy arrays. However, this
required making a copy resulting in 2x memory usage.

I conducted some experiments showing that we can safely
avoid making this copy. Instead, we merely unlink the
shared memory. The memory region will remain accessible
so long as there is an open file descriptor to it. The FD
will be closed when the output VolumeCutout is garbage collected.

In all common use cases I have witnessed, this should result in
the transparent usage of shared memory without the concomitant
memory cost. In the case that a user fills an array with
thousands of VolumeCutouts, they have the option of making a
copy using np.copy and closing the file descriptors manually
or automatically.

author: William Silversmith <william.silversmith@gmail.com>
message:
fix: use concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor vs mp.Pool

multiprocessing.Pool has a longstanding known bug where
childprocesses abruptly dying results in indefinite hanging.
This can happen e.g. if a child process exceeds the memory
limit and is killed by the OS violently.

As of Python 3.3, concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor should
raise a concurrent.futures.process.BrokenProcessPool under those
conditions.

https://docs.python.org/3/library/concurrent.futures.html

author: William Silversmith <william.silversmith@gmail.com>
message:
perf: 1x memory usage for parallel downloads

Previously, I was very conservative and wanted to ensure
that the usage of shared memory was completely invisible
to the end user of downloaded numpy arrays. However, this
required making a copy resulting in 2x memory usage.

I conducted some experiments showing that we can safely
avoid making this copy. Instead, we merely unlink the
shared memory. The memory region will remain accessible
so long as there is an open file descriptor to it. The FD
will be closed when the output VolumeCutout is garbage collected.

In all common use cases I have witnessed, this should result in
the transparent usage of shared memory without the concomitant
memory cost. In the case that a user fills an array with
thousands of VolumeCutouts, they have the option of making a
copy using np.copy and closing the file descriptors manually
or automatically.

message:
fix: use concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor vs mp.Pool (#108)

multiprocessing.Pool has a longstanding known bug where
childprocesses abruptly dying results in indefinite hanging.
This can happen e.g. if a child process exceeds the memory
limit and is killed by the OS violently.

As of Python 3.3, concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor should
raise a concurrent.futures.process.BrokenProcessPool under those
conditions.

https://docs.python.org/3/library/concurrent.futures.html

author: Chris Roat <1053153+chrisroat@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Do not delay creation of metadata when using dask

I originally made this change before I understood the dask ecosystem, and I was desiring to have many volumes'  created in parallel across many workers.

For other output formats (parquet, zarr, etc), the metadata is written at graph creation time, not delayed to run time.  So this change modifies the behavior to be consistent with the rest of the ecosystem.

feat: added cache flag to CloudVolume (#12)

You can now set cache=True to enable reading from disk after downloading.
This is only recommended for jobs less than a few gigabytes, large jobs
will fill up your disk.

Moving the neuroglancer hidden directory to .cloudvolume to finally
achieve indepencence. This can be customized by setting environment
variable CLOUD_VOLUME_DIR.

* fix: removed cache prohibition from 'file' protocol

Will Wong pointed out that 'file' could be used over NFS.

* feat: cached saving and reading of info and provenance

* fix: fix saving provenance files in python3

* chore: eliminate dead broken code

* docs: updated cache flag documentation

Also added support for EmptyRequestException

* test: non-standard cache locations

* fix: error if cache doesn't exist when testing for write access

* merge: fixed merge error with self._storage

* fix: reading json in python3

* feat: check info and provenance cache validity

If not existing do nothing
If info exists, check against source and error if different
  With the exception of volume_size which issues a warning
If provenance exists, check against source and warn if different

* docs: updated cache mismatch instructions

* fix: merge didn't account for new path variable

message:
perf: instant fs based shared memory files + use spare file capability (#334)

Previously we were writing out real files full of zeros,
but a) that takes forever and b) modern OSes support sparse
files (i.e. gigabytes of zeros that take up only a few real bytes).

The following should take advantage of this functionality and be faster.
It should work on Python 2.7 Unix, and Python 3.5+ on Unix and Windows.

References:
  https://stackoverflow.com/questions/8816059/create-file-of-particular-size-in-python
  https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.ftruncate
  https://docs.python.org/2/library/os.html#os.ftruncate

* feat: add use_byte_offsets to cv.mesh.get

    The manifest for sharded is a bit strange in that exists(..., return_byte_offset=True)
    is being called on the server side. To avoid duplicative delay by recomputing the offset
    locations, the manifest breaks encapsulation by returning the shard filename and byte
    offsets. This breaks enapsulation of the shard fetching logic rather severely.

    In order to support fetching meshes in more extraordinary conditions, such as when
    developing a second mesh with different shard parameters while maintaining the older
    mesh for proofreading and visualization while it's generated, we incoroprate a hybrid
    mode that continues to use the manifest, but in order to acquire labels and then fetches
    the labels in bypass mode.

fix: numpy 1.16.0 disallows write=True on string buffers

Convert the immutable string to a bytearray. This incurs an
an additional copy of the chunk. No big deal if the chunk size
is small (e.g. 128x128x64), but if it's large it can be substantial
(e.g. 1024x1024x100).

Resolves #181  (partially)

more intuitive position, compression will change the locations
of the data segments that it is attempting to point to.

message:
fix(ThreadedQueue): ensure processed matches task_done

There's a bug where it's possible for the main thread to proceed after
queue.join() stops blocking butbefore self.processed is incremented,
resulting in a temporary discrepancy of 1. We invert the order of these
operations to ensure that join will not stop blocking until all tasks
are accounted for.

author: Stefan Vigerske <svigerske@gams.com>
message:
fix to ipoptr (contributed by Anirban Mukherjee and Jelmer Ypma)

Jelmer suggested that I try changing these lines in R/ipoptr.R

# build ipoptr object
    ret <- list( "x0"=x0,
                 "eval_f"=eval_f_wrapper,
                 "eval_grad_f"=eval_grad_f_wrapper,
                 "lower_bounds"=lb,
                 "upper_bounds"=ub,
                 "eval_g"=eval_g_wrapper,
                 "eval_jac_g"=eval_jac_g_wrapper,
                 "constraint_lower_bounds"=constraint_lb,
                 "constraint_upper_bounds"=constraint_ub,
                 "eval_jac_g_structure"=eval_jac_g_structure,
                 "eval_h"=eval_h_wrapper,
                 "eval_h_structure"=eval_h_structure,
                 "options"=get.option.types(opts) )

to

# build ipoptr object
    ret <- list( "x0"=x0,
                 "eval_f"=eval_f_wrapper,
                 "eval_grad_f"=eval_grad_f_wrapper,
                 "lower_bounds"=lb,
                 "upper_bounds"=ub,
                 "eval_g"=eval_g_wrapper,
                 "eval_jac_g"=eval_jac_g_wrapper,
                 "constraint_lower_bounds"=constraint_lb,
                 "constraint_upper_bounds"=constraint_ub,
                 "eval_jac_g_structure"=eval_jac_g_structure,
                 "eval_h"=eval_h_wrapper,
                 "eval_h_structure"=eval_h_structure,
                 "options"=get.option.types(opts),

                 "environment" = new.env() )

In ipopt.r I see one additional element in the ret list
("ipoptr_environment"=ipoptr_environment). I first left that in and
added the element/argument suggested ("environment" = new.env()) to get:

    # build ipoptr object
    ret <- list( "x0"=x0,
                 "eval_f"=eval_f_wrapper,
                 "eval_grad_f"=eval_grad_f_wrapper,
                 "lower_bounds"=lb,
                 "upper_bounds"=ub,
                 "eval_g"=eval_g_wrapper,
                 "eval_jac_g"=eval_jac_g_wrapper,
                 "constraint_lower_bounds"=constraint_lb,
                 "constraint_upper_bounds"=constraint_ub,
                 "eval_jac_g_structure"=eval_jac_g_structure,
                 "eval_h"=eval_h_wrapper,
                 "eval_h_structure"=eval_h_structure,
                 "options"=get.option.types(opts),
                 "ipoptr_environment"=ipoptr_environment,
                  "environment" = new.env() )

Installing this from R as a package worked as expected.

However, revision 8 on R-forge says that Jelmer removed
ipoptr_environment because of a conflict with data.table. (I am not sure
why ipopt 3.11.3, which I downloaded last week, still has this argument
given Jelmer's revision dated March 2012.)

https://r-forge.r-project.org/scm/viewvc.php/pkg/R/ipoptr.R?view=markup&root=ipoptr

I tried removing the ipoptr_environment argument but got the following
error message:

Error: is.environment(x$ipoptr_environment) is not TRUE

It did not seem that ipoptr_environment was doing much. So I went into
is.ipopt.R and changed line 18 which checks if "ipoptr_environment" is
an R environment, to a check if "environment" is an environment.

I changed

stopifnot( is.environment(x$ipoptr_environment) )

to

stopifnot( is.environment(x$environment) )

This works as expected on my system. Ipoptr loads and gives the right
solution in the examples.

Summary: in ipopt.R I commented out the argument
("ipoptr_environment"=ipoptr_environment) and added the argument
("environment" = new.env() ). In is.ipopt.R I changed line 18 which
checks if ipoptr_environment is an environment to a check for
environment being an environment. For redundancy I am attaching both .R
files to this email.

message:
apply changes from pull request !5: support custom algorithm development

See https://github.com/coin-or/Ipopt/pull/5:
This pull request mainly consists of a reorganization of the AlgorithmBuilder class to allow easier customization of the Ipopt algorithm. In particular, we wanted to make use of the code that creates the SymLinearSolver object to implement our own SymLinearSolver without copy-pasting everything in AlgorithmBuilder.
AlgorithmBuilder::BuildBasicAlgorithm now consists of 8 method calls that build the core components passed into the arguments of the IpoptAlgorithm class. These calls are ordered based on any dependencies they might have. In addition, all code for creating the PDSystemSolver, AugSystemSolver, and SymLinearSolver has been moved into separate factory methods.
Also, included is a change to install a few more header files with Ipopt. Some of these are required to subclass AlgorithmBuilder, and the others are simply some matrix types that we require.

CHANGELOG:

09 March 2012, version 0.8.4:

    * Included additional variables to the object that is returned from ipoptr (thanks to Michael Schedl). These are:
            z_L         : final values for the lower bound multipliers
            z_U         : final values for the upper bound multipliers
            constraints : final values for the constraints
            lambda      : final values for the Lagrange mulipliers
      After solving the NLP using
            R> res <- ipoptr( ... )
      They can be accessed using
            R> res$z_L
            R> res$z_U
            R> res$constraints
            R> res$lambda

    * Removed ipoptr_environment as argument in ipoptr because it wasn't useful and it caused undesired behaviour in 
      combination with the data.table package (thanks to Florian Oswald for reporting).

author: Stefan Vigerske <svigerske@gams.com>
message:
apply changes from pull request !5: support custom algorithm development

See https://github.com/coin-or/Ipopt/pull/5:
This pull request mainly consists of a reorganization of the AlgorithmBuilder class to allow easier customization of the Ipopt algorithm. In particular, we wanted to make use of the code that creates the SymLinearSolver object to implement our own SymLinearSolver without copy-pasting everything in AlgorithmBuilder.
AlgorithmBuilder::BuildBasicAlgorithm now consists of 8 method calls that build the core components passed into the arguments of the IpoptAlgorithm class. These calls are ordered based on any dependencies they might have. In addition, all code for creating the PDSystemSolver, AugSystemSolver, and SymLinearSolver has been moved into separate factory methods.
Also, included is a change to install a few more header files with Ipopt. Some of these are required to subclass AlgorithmBuilder, and the others are simply some matrix types that we require.

author: Stefan Vigerske <svigerske@gams.com>
message:
change default for ma97_print_level to -1

Some e-mail exchange on this topic:

On 11/12/2015 11:48 AM, Jonathan Hogg wrote:
> The system solved by MA97 changes each iteration, with diagonal entries
> in the (1,1) block becoming more extreme towards 0 and +infinity [give
> or take the diagonal entries of the Hessian] depending on whether the
> associated constraint is active or not. This is what I'd expect to be
> causing the singular error messages at some iterations and not at others
> - it is perfectly normal for some problems (and by singular here we mean
> effectively numerically singular rather than structurally or in exact
> arithmetic).
>
> IIRC Ipopt just takes a singular error return as a signal to increase
> regularization of the system in the (1,1) block and then tries again.
> Hence it is probably just a case of needing a patch to tell MA97 not to
> print error messages where the user can see them :P.

Stefan Vigerske, 18 December 2015:
I guess we could suppress all MA97 messages in Ipopt by changing
ma97_print_level to a negative number. Currently it defaults to 0, which
means "error and warning messages only".
I'm not sure that disabling error messages by default is a good thing to do.
If a numerical singular system is not a really serious error, couldn't
one change the message to appear only on print level 1 ("limited
diagnostic printing") or higher?

Jonathan Hogg:
The thing is, it /is/ a serious error for the linear solver - it can't
really guarantee much about the quality of the solution it will deliver.
So it needs to stay as a printed error by default or most users of the code.
However as Ipopt detects the error and fixes it by regularizing the
problem, it's not a serious error as far as Ipopt is concerned.
I think the solution of setting the ma97 print level to off and reporting
any "unhandled" error returns via an Ipopt error message is probably the
best way to go.

author: Stefan Vigerske <svigerske@gams.com>
message:
fix to ipoptr (contributed by Anirban Mukherjee and Jelmer Ypma)

Jelmer suggested that I try changing these lines in R/ipoptr.R

# build ipoptr object
    ret <- list( "x0"=x0,
                 "eval_f"=eval_f_wrapper,
                 "eval_grad_f"=eval_grad_f_wrapper,
                 "lower_bounds"=lb,
                 "upper_bounds"=ub,
                 "eval_g"=eval_g_wrapper,
                 "eval_jac_g"=eval_jac_g_wrapper,
                 "constraint_lower_bounds"=constraint_lb,
                 "constraint_upper_bounds"=constraint_ub,
                 "eval_jac_g_structure"=eval_jac_g_structure,
                 "eval_h"=eval_h_wrapper,
                 "eval_h_structure"=eval_h_structure,
                 "options"=get.option.types(opts) )

to

# build ipoptr object
    ret <- list( "x0"=x0,
                 "eval_f"=eval_f_wrapper,
                 "eval_grad_f"=eval_grad_f_wrapper,
                 "lower_bounds"=lb,
                 "upper_bounds"=ub,
                 "eval_g"=eval_g_wrapper,
                 "eval_jac_g"=eval_jac_g_wrapper,
                 "constraint_lower_bounds"=constraint_lb,
                 "constraint_upper_bounds"=constraint_ub,
                 "eval_jac_g_structure"=eval_jac_g_structure,
                 "eval_h"=eval_h_wrapper,
                 "eval_h_structure"=eval_h_structure,
                 "options"=get.option.types(opts),

                 "environment" = new.env() )

In ipopt.r I see one additional element in the ret list
("ipoptr_environment"=ipoptr_environment). I first left that in and
added the element/argument suggested ("environment" = new.env()) to get:

    # build ipoptr object
    ret <- list( "x0"=x0,
                 "eval_f"=eval_f_wrapper,
                 "eval_grad_f"=eval_grad_f_wrapper,
                 "lower_bounds"=lb,
                 "upper_bounds"=ub,
                 "eval_g"=eval_g_wrapper,
                 "eval_jac_g"=eval_jac_g_wrapper,
                 "constraint_lower_bounds"=constraint_lb,
                 "constraint_upper_bounds"=constraint_ub,
                 "eval_jac_g_structure"=eval_jac_g_structure,
                 "eval_h"=eval_h_wrapper,
                 "eval_h_structure"=eval_h_structure,
                 "options"=get.option.types(opts),
                 "ipoptr_environment"=ipoptr_environment,
                  "environment" = new.env() )

Installing this from R as a package worked as expected.

However, revision 8 on R-forge says that Jelmer removed
ipoptr_environment because of a conflict with data.table. (I am not sure
why ipopt 3.11.3, which I downloaded last week, still has this argument
given Jelmer's revision dated March 2012.)

https://r-forge.r-project.org/scm/viewvc.php/pkg/R/ipoptr.R?view=markup&root=ipoptr

I tried removing the ipoptr_environment argument but got the following
error message:

Error: is.environment(x$ipoptr_environment) is not TRUE

It did not seem that ipoptr_environment was doing much. So I went into
is.ipopt.R and changed line 18 which checks if "ipoptr_environment" is
an R environment, to a check if "environment" is an environment.

I changed

stopifnot( is.environment(x$ipoptr_environment) )

to

stopifnot( is.environment(x$environment) )

This works as expected on my system. Ipoptr loads and gives the right
solution in the examples.

Summary: in ipopt.R I commented out the argument
("ipoptr_environment"=ipoptr_environment) and added the argument
("environment" = new.env() ). In is.ipopt.R I changed line 18 which
checks if ipoptr_environment is an environment to a check for
environment being an environment. For redundancy I am attaching both .R
files to this email.

author: Stefan Vigerske <svigerske@gams.com>
message:
by Toni Kelman: automate some steps for building mex files on Mac and Windows

This adds get.Gnumex to /Ipopt/contrib/MatlabInterface along with a patch
I wrote to make Gnumex work on Win64 Matlab.

Gnumex doesn't need to build any executables, it runs from inside
Matlab. It comes with some mexw32 files, and part of my patch tries to
build the mexw64 equivalents from inside Matlab (if 64 bit), or uses a
different workaround if that fails. I added a gnumex target in
Makefile.in to open an instance of Matlab and run Gnumex (or echo a
warning with instructions if the user hasn't run get.Gnumex yet) with
some of the options filled out to recommended settings. If Cygwin and/or
MinGW are installed in default locations, the user should only need to
click "Make options file" then exit the new instance of Matlab (so we
know Gnumex is finished).

The new mexopts target in Makefile.in makes the Mac or Windows
modifications to mexopts.sh or mexopts.bat. I added it as a recursive
make call in the $(TARGET) rule, since adding it to the dependencies
would make "mexopts" show up on the compilation command line from "$^".
We could alternately have "make mexopts" always be a manual step for Mac
and Windows users.

For Mac, if there is not currently a mexopts.sh file in the Matlab
interface build directory, I look at the default one, test if the
hardcoded $SDKROOT path actually exists, and if not I make a copy with
all references to $SDKROOT removed.

For Windows, I give a warning if no mexopts.bat file is found in the
Matlab interface build directory. This warning message may take a lot of
scrolling to find unfortunately, if the default setup results in really
long error messages from mex. If there is a mexopts.bat in the build
directory, I add $(LIBS) to GM_ADD_LIBS, change COMPILER=gcc to
COMPILER=g++, and GM_MEXLANG=c to GM_MEXLANG=cxx. I need to modify -L
flags from $(LIBS) to Windows format directories, although forward
slashes work and prevent having to double/quadruple/octuple backslashes
for future sed calls. I do this using "cygpath -m" on $(libdir) and
/usr/lib in Cygwin, or using a fairly ugly cmd /c DOS for-do-@echo call
in MinGW (only on libdir).

An annoyance in Cygwin is that due to the alternatives system, g++ is a
symbolic link to either g++-4 or g++-3. This causes "Access is denied"
errors when linking mex files, so on Cygwin I use g++-4 for COMPILER, or
g++-3 if the former is not on the path, or g++ if neither g++-4 or g++-3
is on the path.

Results:
Linux - no change, except more output to the screen when going through the no-op make mexopts.

Mac - working mex file when configured with --disable-shared, but
crashes Matlab without. The shared-library version gives a malloc error,
"pointer being freed was not allocated," in
IpoptOptions::useQuasiNewton, Ipopt::OptionsList::GetStringValue,
std::string::assign. This is probably a libstdc++ incompatibility issue.

MinGW32 - works very nicely with no configure flags needed (../configure
&& make install test && cd Ipopt/contrib/MatlabInterface/src && make
gnumex install && echo done)

MinGW64 - works with the configure flag ADD_FFLAGS=-static-libgcc, this
prevents a "multiple definition of `_Unwind_SjLj_Unregister'" error when
using the TDM-GCC distribution of MinGW64.

Cygwin - compiles mex file successfully, but freezes Matlab when
configured with --disable-shared, crashes Matlab without. The
freeze/crash is extremely difficult to debug, I couldn't even get any
output by adding a printf at the very beginning of mexFunction in
ipopt.cpp.

can also catch the exceptions, etc...)

Cheers,

Carl.

author: Gabe Hackebeil <gabe.hackebeil@gmail.com>
message:
Updating Ipopt restoration phase code for better handling of NLPs that originally consist of compound component spaces (e.g., CompoundMatrix, CompoundVector). **Note: NLPs coming from executables like AMPL ipopt do not consist of compound entries so I suspect this case is not common. These changes should have absolutely no numerical effect on algorithm convergence. They simply prevent errors from occurring inside the IpoptCalculatedQuantities class for the restoration phase NLP when the original NLP's component spaces consist of CompoundMatrix / CompoundVector. A more detailed explanation follows:

The restoration phase NLP wraps certain components from the original NLP (e.g., x, JacC, JacD) inside compound component spaces due to the addition of positive and negative slack variables. For those component spaces that are not affected by the addition of these variables (e.g., c, d), the restoration phase NLP uses the original NLP's component spaces. Therefore, inside the IpoptCalculatedQuantities class (when the original NLP used non-compound spaces), this would result in mixed compound/non-compound linear algebra operations. This makes the code very difficult to debug when the original NLP used compound components (and even causes assertion errors for a few edge cases in the linear algebra routines). The fix is to simply place the unmodified component spaces for the restoration phase NLP inside trivial singleton compound components in order to preserve the same compound nesting across linear algebra operations.

author: Tony Kelman <kelman@berkeley.edu>
message:
Additional checks of initial point input and callback function outputs
- Error if initial point is complex or sparse
- Error if any callback returns complex value
- Error if gradient or constraint does not return a double
- Convert sparse objective, gradient (done in R2133), or constraint to full
- Convert non-double Jacobian structure, Hessian structure, Jacobian, or Hessian to double

This fixes a segfault on large problems if structure callbacks return Matlab logical datatypes (A ~= 0), the line copymemory(mxGetPr(ptr),x,nnz) in the SparseMatrix constructor was going past the valid range of the mxGetPr(ptr) array since logicals are smaller than doubles. This was still giving correct behavior for problems with few enough nonzeros not to segfault, since only the row and column indices are used from the structure matrices and it didn't matter that the values contained garbage.

author: Stefan Vigerske <svigerske@gams.com>
message:
by Toni Kelman: automate some steps for building mex files on Mac and Windows

This adds get.Gnumex to /Ipopt/contrib/MatlabInterface along with a patch
I wrote to make Gnumex work on Win64 Matlab.

Gnumex doesn't need to build any executables, it runs from inside
Matlab. It comes with some mexw32 files, and part of my patch tries to
build the mexw64 equivalents from inside Matlab (if 64 bit), or uses a
different workaround if that fails. I added a gnumex target in
Makefile.in to open an instance of Matlab and run Gnumex (or echo a
warning with instructions if the user hasn't run get.Gnumex yet) with
some of the options filled out to recommended settings. If Cygwin and/or
MinGW are installed in default locations, the user should only need to
click "Make options file" then exit the new instance of Matlab (so we
know Gnumex is finished).

The new mexopts target in Makefile.in makes the Mac or Windows
modifications to mexopts.sh or mexopts.bat. I added it as a recursive
make call in the $(TARGET) rule, since adding it to the dependencies
would make "mexopts" show up on the compilation command line from "$^".
We could alternately have "make mexopts" always be a manual step for Mac
and Windows users.

For Mac, if there is not currently a mexopts.sh file in the Matlab
interface build directory, I look at the default one, test if the
hardcoded $SDKROOT path actually exists, and if not I make a copy with
all references to $SDKROOT removed.

For Windows, I give a warning if no mexopts.bat file is found in the
Matlab interface build directory. This warning message may take a lot of
scrolling to find unfortunately, if the default setup results in really
long error messages from mex. If there is a mexopts.bat in the build
directory, I add $(LIBS) to GM_ADD_LIBS, change COMPILER=gcc to
COMPILER=g++, and GM_MEXLANG=c to GM_MEXLANG=cxx. I need to modify -L
flags from $(LIBS) to Windows format directories, although forward
slashes work and prevent having to double/quadruple/octuple backslashes
for future sed calls. I do this using "cygpath -m" on $(libdir) and
/usr/lib in Cygwin, or using a fairly ugly cmd /c DOS for-do-@echo call
in MinGW (only on libdir).

An annoyance in Cygwin is that due to the alternatives system, g++ is a
symbolic link to either g++-4 or g++-3. This causes "Access is denied"
errors when linking mex files, so on Cygwin I use g++-4 for COMPILER, or
g++-3 if the former is not on the path, or g++ if neither g++-4 or g++-3
is on the path.

Results:
Linux - no change, except more output to the screen when going through the no-op make mexopts.

Mac - working mex file when configured with --disable-shared, but
crashes Matlab without. The shared-library version gives a malloc error,
"pointer being freed was not allocated," in
IpoptOptions::useQuasiNewton, Ipopt::OptionsList::GetStringValue,
std::string::assign. This is probably a libstdc++ incompatibility issue.

MinGW32 - works very nicely with no configure flags needed (../configure
&& make install test && cd Ipopt/contrib/MatlabInterface/src && make
gnumex install && echo done)

MinGW64 - works with the configure flag ADD_FFLAGS=-static-libgcc, this
prevents a "multiple definition of `_Unwind_SjLj_Unregister'" error when
using the TDM-GCC distribution of MinGW64.

Cygwin - compiles mex file successfully, but freezes Matlab when
configured with --disable-shared, crashes Matlab without. The
freeze/crash is extremely difficult to debug, I couldn't even get any
output by adding a printf at the very beginning of mexFunction in
ipopt.cpp.

author: Stefan Vigerske <svigerske@gams.com>
message:
contributed by Tony Kelman: improvements to Matlab recognition in configure and build of Matlab interface

Following Tony's description of this patch:

Overall, I see that configure has a section regarding the Matlab interface,
but much of the time (especially on Windows or Mac) it does not do the job
entirely and users have to make manual modifications to the Matlab interface
Makefile along with mexopts.sh (.bat on Windows). My goal with this patch is
to at least eliminate the need to modify the Makefile, for as many cases as
possible.

The existing configure section for the Matlab interface tries to
automatically look for the Matlab installation location with a "which"
call, but many recent Matlab versions (for Linux) have moved away from adding
the $MATLAB_HOME/bin directory to the system path, and towards adding just a
few symbolic links in /usr/local/bin. So mexext is rarely on the path
anymore, but matlab frequently is - often as a symbolic link. I've changed the
"which" commands to look for matlab accordingly, and in the case of
symbolic links, read where they point to ($MATLAB_HOME/bin/matlab). I'm not sure
whether my `ls -l "$mexpath" | awk '{print $NF}'` is more or less
preferable/portable than using readlink. I also added a few quotes
anywhere $MATLAB_HOME gets used, in case the Matlab path has spaces in it (common
in Windows - could get or require the user to provide the short PROGRA~1
style name, but I don't think it's necessary).

On Windows, Matlab is more frequently on the path. The behavior of
"which" is inconsistent between Cygwin and MSYS for executable names: Cygwin
returns the location without the .exe extension if the input does not end with
.exe, whereas in MSYS "which matlab" returns "/c/path/to/matlab.exe" or
similar.
If you ask for "which matlab.exe" on the other hand, both Cygwin and
MSYS return the location including the .exe at the end. So I've added $EXEEXT
in the "which" command and the sed call that removes /bin/matlab.exe from
the end of the "which" result. This will make no difference for Linux or Mac
users, when $EXEEXT is empty.

On Windows, the mex and mexext utilities are batch files, so we need to
add .bat in order to find them. MSYS can't execute batch files natively, so
I use cmd /c to call mexext.bat for MinGW.

The mex compiler doesn't understand Apple-style flags like "-framework
vecLib." Ray Zimmerman's "Ipopt on Mac OS X" wiki page has a step where
he says to remove "-framework vecLib" from the LIBS line of the Matlab
interface Makefile, and to add it to LDFLAGS in mexopts.sh. I've added a
sed call in contrib/MatlabInterface/src/Makefile.in to remove it from LIBS
automatically. Rather than adding it to LDFLAGS in mexopts.sh, it can be
added to LDFLAGS in Makefile.in. I've added an AC_SUBST variable to do
that, defined in configure by grepping $BLAS_LIBS and $LAPACK_LIBS for
"-framework vecLib". This way the user doesn't have to mess with mexopts.sh as
often.

There can still be problems on Mac since Mathworks hardcodes an expected
Xcode version in $SDKROOT, which may not be installed. That's not
necessarily configure's job to fix, but it could be. I have a
post-configure script that copies the default mexopts.sh from its location in
$MATLAB_HOME/bin, tests whether or not the expected $SDKROOT directory
exists, and makes the necessary modifications if it doesn't.

On Windows, mex doesn't recognize the -cxx flag. I get rid of it
selectively using a new AM_CONDITIONAL, MEX_WINDOWS. I also use the same conditional
to modify the setting of MEX to call Matlab's included Perl on
$(MATLAB_HOME)/bin/mex.pl. There are a few more quotes and a CYGPATH_W
call in there to handle Matlab paths with spaces, and paths returned from
"which" that are in /cygdrive/c/path format. I was a little worried about the
win32 in the path to Perl, but turns out even 64-bit Matlab includes a 32-bit
version of Perl at that path.

I've tested this set of changes pretty extensively on Linux, Mac, Win32,
Win64, Cygwin, MinGW32, MinGW64, with and without Matlab, various
combinations of specifying --with-matlab-home as a configure flag with
different directory formats, or letting configure find Matlab via
"which."
It works as expected, or at least better than the existing version, in
every test I could come up with.

On Windows this patch by itself is not enough to get a functioning mex
file, but the only missing piece should be mexopts.bat generated by Gnumex
(http://sourceforge.net/projects/gnumex/) then modified appropriately.
The post-configure script I have does all this, but I imagine automatically
downloading Gnumex could be problematic due to the differing licenses.
It might be too OS-specific to add as a ThirdParty/Gnumex/get.Gnumex, but I
could contribute the remaining pieces in that form if there's interest.

author: Stefan Vigerske <svigerske@gams.com>
message:
contributed by Tony Kelman: improvements to Matlab recognition in configure and build of Matlab interface

Following Tony's description of this patch:

Overall, I see that configure has a section regarding the Matlab interface,
but much of the time (especially on Windows or Mac) it does not do the job
entirely and users have to make manual modifications to the Matlab interface
Makefile along with mexopts.sh (.bat on Windows). My goal with this patch is
to at least eliminate the need to modify the Makefile, for as many cases as
possible.

The existing configure section for the Matlab interface tries to
automatically look for the Matlab installation location with a "which"
call, but many recent Matlab versions (for Linux) have moved away from adding
the $MATLAB_HOME/bin directory to the system path, and towards adding just a
few symbolic links in /usr/local/bin. So mexext is rarely on the path
anymore, but matlab frequently is - often as a symbolic link. I've changed the
"which" commands to look for matlab accordingly, and in the case of
symbolic links, read where they point to ($MATLAB_HOME/bin/matlab). I'm not sure
whether my `ls -l "$mexpath" | awk '{print $NF}'` is more or less
preferable/portable than using readlink. I also added a few quotes
anywhere $MATLAB_HOME gets used, in case the Matlab path has spaces in it (common
in Windows - could get or require the user to provide the short PROGRA~1
style name, but I don't think it's necessary).

On Windows, Matlab is more frequently on the path. The behavior of
"which" is inconsistent between Cygwin and MSYS for executable names: Cygwin
returns the location without the .exe extension if the input does not end with
.exe, whereas in MSYS "which matlab" returns "/c/path/to/matlab.exe" or
similar.
If you ask for "which matlab.exe" on the other hand, both Cygwin and
MSYS return the location including the .exe at the end. So I've added $EXEEXT
in the "which" command and the sed call that removes /bin/matlab.exe from
the end of the "which" result. This will make no difference for Linux or Mac
users, when $EXEEXT is empty.

On Windows, the mex and mexext utilities are batch files, so we need to
add .bat in order to find them. MSYS can't execute batch files natively, so
I use cmd /c to call mexext.bat for MinGW.

The mex compiler doesn't understand Apple-style flags like "-framework
vecLib." Ray Zimmerman's "Ipopt on Mac OS X" wiki page has a step where
he says to remove "-framework vecLib" from the LIBS line of the Matlab
interface Makefile, and to add it to LDFLAGS in mexopts.sh. I've added a
sed call in contrib/MatlabInterface/src/Makefile.in to remove it from LIBS
automatically. Rather than adding it to LDFLAGS in mexopts.sh, it can be
added to LDFLAGS in Makefile.in. I've added an AC_SUBST variable to do
that, defined in configure by grepping $BLAS_LIBS and $LAPACK_LIBS for
"-framework vecLib". This way the user doesn't have to mess with mexopts.sh as
often.

There can still be problems on Mac since Mathworks hardcodes an expected
Xcode version in $SDKROOT, which may not be installed. That's not
necessarily configure's job to fix, but it could be. I have a
post-configure script that copies the default mexopts.sh from its location in
$MATLAB_HOME/bin, tests whether or not the expected $SDKROOT directory
exists, and makes the necessary modifications if it doesn't.

On Windows, mex doesn't recognize the -cxx flag. I get rid of it
selectively using a new AM_CONDITIONAL, MEX_WINDOWS. I also use the same conditional
to modify the setting of MEX to call Matlab's included Perl on
$(MATLAB_HOME)/bin/mex.pl. There are a few more quotes and a CYGPATH_W
call in there to handle Matlab paths with spaces, and paths returned from
"which" that are in /cygdrive/c/path format. I was a little worried about the
win32 in the path to Perl, but turns out even 64-bit Matlab includes a 32-bit
version of Perl at that path.

I've tested this set of changes pretty extensively on Linux, Mac, Win32,
Win64, Cygwin, MinGW32, MinGW64, with and without Matlab, various
combinations of specifying --with-matlab-home as a configure flag with
different directory formats, or letting configure find Matlab via
"which."
It works as expected, or at least better than the existing version, in
every test I could come up with.

On Windows this patch by itself is not enough to get a functioning mex
file, but the only missing piece should be mexopts.bat generated by Gnumex
(http://sourceforge.net/projects/gnumex/) then modified appropriately.
The post-configure script I have does all this, but I imagine automatically
downloading Gnumex could be problematic due to the differing licenses.
It might be too OS-specific to add as a ThirdParty/Gnumex/get.Gnumex, but I
could contribute the remaining pieces in that form if there's interest.

author: Kevin Kofler <kofler@dagopt.com>
message:
Fix rare use-after-free in IpSpralSolverInterface

src/Algorithm/LinearSolvers/IpSpralSolverInterface.cpp
(SpralSolverInterface::MultiSolve): Fix a corner case where attempting
to solve a second system with the same structurally singular matrix
would end up trying to use an old numeric factorization (fkeep_) using
data from an already freed symbolic factorization (akeep_). This was
really hard to debug. What was going on was that, if
spral_ssids_analyse_ptr32 found the matrix to be structurally singular,
Ipopt would return early, without calling spral_ssids_factor_ptr32, so
fkeep_ would still point to the old data. Then later, if the same matrix
was to be reused (new_matrix=FALSE), Ipopt would try to call
spral_ssids_solve on that invalid factorization. The fix is twofold:
1. Before calling spral_ssids_analyse_ptr32, we have to call
   spral_ssids_free so that both akeep_ and fkeep_ are freed and reset to
   NULL, because spral_ssids_analyse_ptr32 sees and frees only akeep_. And
2. Before calling spral_ssids_solve, we have to check whether fkeep_ is
   NULL, in which case we return (again) with SYMSOLVER_SINGULAR.

author: Gabe Hackerbeil <gabe.hackebeil@gmail.com>
message:
Updating Ipopt restoration phase code for better handling of NLPs that originally consist of compound component spaces (e.g., CompoundMatrix, CompoundVector). **Note: NLPs coming from executables like AMPL ipopt do not consist of compound entries so I suspect this case is not common. These changes should have absolutely no numerical effect on algorithm convergence. They simply prevent errors from occurring inside the IpoptCalculatedQuantities class for the restoration phase NLP when the original NLP's component spaces consist of CompoundMatrix / CompoundVector. A more detailed explanation follows:

The restoration phase NLP wraps certain components from the original NLP (e.g., x, JacC, JacD) inside compound component spaces due to the addition of positive and negative slack variables. For those component spaces that are not affected by the addition of these variables (e.g., c, d), the restoration phase NLP uses the original NLP's component spaces. Therefore, inside the IpoptCalculatedQuantities class (when the original NLP used non-compound spaces), this would result in mixed compound/non-compound linear algebra operations. This makes the code very difficult to debug when the original NLP used compound components (and even causes assertion errors for a few edge cases in the linear algebra routines). The fix is to simply place the unmodified component spaces for the restoration phase NLP inside trivial singleton compound components in order to preserve the same compound nesting across linear algebra operations.

author: Kevin Kofler <kofler@dagopt.com>
message:
Fix rare use-after-free in IpSpralSolverInterface

src/Algorithm/LinearSolvers/IpSpralSolverInterface.cpp
(SpralSolverInterface::MultiSolve): Fix a corner case where attempting
to solve a second system with the same structurally singular matrix
would end up trying to use an old numeric factorization (fkeep_) using
data from an already freed symbolic factorization (akeep_). This was
really hard to debug. What was going on was that, if
spral_ssids_analyse_ptr32 found the matrix to be structurally singular,
Ipopt would return early, without calling spral_ssids_factor_ptr32, so
fkeep_ would still point to the old data. Then later, if the same matrix
was to be reused (new_matrix=FALSE), Ipopt would try to call
spral_ssids_solve on that invalid factorization. The fix is twofold:
1. Before calling spral_ssids_analyse_ptr32, we have to call
   spral_ssids_free so that both akeep_ and fkeep_ are freed and reset to
   NULL, because spral_ssids_analyse_ptr32 sees and frees only akeep_. And
2. Before calling spral_ssids_solve, we have to check whether fkeep_ is
   NULL, in which case we return (again) with SYMSOLVER_SINGULAR.

In this case, setting the entries in full_z_L|U for the fixed variables failed, since the implementation

This commit works around a segmentation fault in optimized mode by adding an implementation for the case
that y_c is homogeneous.

author: Tony Kelman <kelman@berkeley.edu>
message:
Additional checks of initial point input and callback function outputs
- Error if initial point is complex or sparse
- Error if any callback returns complex value
- Error if gradient or constraint does not return a double
- Convert sparse objective, gradient (done in R2133), or constraint to full
- Convert non-double Jacobian structure, Hessian structure, Jacobian, or Hessian to double

This fixes a segfault on large problems if structure callbacks return Matlab logical datatypes (A ~= 0), the line copymemory(mxGetPr(ptr),x,nnz) in the SparseMatrix constructor was going past the valid range of the mxGetPr(ptr) array since logicals are smaller than doubles. This was still giving correct behavior for problems with few enough nonzeros not to segfault, since only the row and column indices are used from the structure matrices and it didn't matter that the values contained garbage.

changes. The next step is to update the rest of the documentation
